findings.where: Step 9 (Seen from the boat), SHOW text
findings.what: "Seen from your boat, your own arrow is turned round and added to everything, so your boat sits still and the bank slides west." is 25 words, passive and chains three clauses, and the next sentence stacks three appositives ("moves at 8j − 6i, 10 knots, its relative velocity"); split into short active sentences, e.g. "From your boat, add your own arrow turned round to everything. Your boat then sits still. The bank slides west. The vessel moves at 8j − 6i. That is its relative velocity, 10 knots."

findings.where: Step 7 (The boat and the stream), SHOW text and read; also DRAW.drift's description
findings.what: "Over the ground it moves along the two arrows nose to tail" says the boat travels along both arrows in turn, an L-shaped path, when it moves along their sum, the diagonal; say "it moves along the sum of the two arrows, at 5 m/s".

The meter with red on A reads A minus B, then "A displacement behaves like that. AB is b − a" pairs it with the opposite order, which invites the sign mistake this lesson is built to stop; put the red lead on B and the black on A so it reads end minus start, or say plainly that the meter's order is the other way round.
It says BC "is 2 × AB" without ever giving AB = 2i + 1j, so Dan has to work it out or find it in the readout; add "AB is 2i + 1j." before it.

"They also share B, so the three points lie on one line" does not say why sharing a point matters (parallel steps alone could sit on two separate lines); the explain has that sentence, and the screen has room for it.

findings.where: Step 6 (Which point is in line?), readout band
findings.what: The readout is labelled "BD" and "BD is 3 × AB", but no point D is named in the task or the picture; name the picked point D, or label the readout "from B".
"The arrows meet at a right angle" is ambiguous here, because the heading and the stream do not meet at a right angle; name the pair, e.g. "The stream and the track across meet at a right angle."

Lower-case a and b appear in "the move AB is b − a" without saying they are the arrows from the origin to A and B, and the brief's term "position vector" is never named, though he will meet it in every text after this; add "a, the arrow from the origin to A, is its position vector."

findings.where: Step 12 task (i4.a1-360-light-end.png) and step 7 text at 360 px
findings.what: Numbers split from their units across lines ("It makes 4 / m/s, and the stream runs at 3 / m/s"); bind number and unit with a no-break space.

findings.where: Step 9 demonstration (film-s8, about 1.0 s to 2.2 s)
findings.what: The "over the ground: you 6i knots, vessel 8j knots" readout fades in and out again within about a second, before the view switches, which is too short to read; hold it until the switch or leave it out.
The grid fills only the left 60% or so of the picture at 360 px, leaving the right third empty and the drawing off-centre; centre it or give it the width.

The screen gives the rule and the answer but not why a − b runs from b's nose to a's nose; the read version's "Go out along b, then along a − b, and you land on a" fits within the word budget and belongs on screen too.
It opens "Velocities take away the same way" but then teaches only adding (ground = heading + stream); say where the taking away is: the heading you need is the track you want minus the stream.

The brief promised one screen on steam meeting a moving turbine blade and a warning against the "join the dots" mistake on a course to steer; the blade gets one sentence in the practice and "join the dots" is missing, though both suit Dan's marine engineering path.
